nodes.title: gh release list -R https://github.com/cli/cli/ -> error
nodes.body:
### Describe the bug

`gh release list -R https://github.com/cli/cli/` gives back:

```
non-200 OK status code: 401 Unauthorized body: "{\r\n  \"message\": \"Requires authentication\",\r\n  \"documentation_url\": \"https://docs.github.com/rest\",\r\n  \"status\": \"401\"\r\n}"
```
Instead of listing available releases.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.102.0
```

Running on
```
DISTRIB_ID=Ubuntu
DISTRIB_RELEASE=26.04
DISTRIB_CODENAME=resolute
DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION="Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS"
```

1. Download `gh` using any browser from "https://github.com/cli/cli/release"
2. Install `gh` using `dpkg -i gh_2.102.0_linux_amd64.deb`

nodes.title: gh pr merge --squash can land the commit while the pull request stays open
nodes.body:
### Describe the bug

`gh pr merge --squash` can update the base branch with the squash commit and leave the pull request open, with no merged event and no workflow run for that commit. The same pull request merged from the website behaves correctly, and three earlier pull requests merged with the same command behaved correctly, so the failure is intermittent.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.102.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not reproducible on demand: the same command succeeded on three earlier pull requests in the same repository and failed on one, with the same ruleset and the same pull request state.

1. Merge a pull request with `gh pr merge <number> --squash --match-head-commit <sha> --body-file <file>`, against a base branch protected by a ruleset that requires a pull request and allows only the squash merge method.
2. Run `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit` — the pull request still reports `state: OPEN`, `mergedAt: null` and a null merge commit.
3. Run `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>` — the same, and `merge_commit_sha` still holds the synthetic test-merge commit.
4. Run `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>/timeline` — there is no `merged` event.
5. Run `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<base>` — the base branch does point at the new squash commit, whose message carries the pull request reference and the body passed with `--body-file`.
6. Run `gh run list --branch <base>` — no workflow run exists for that commit.

### Expected vs actual behavior

The pull request is marked as merged, a `merged` event appears in its timeline, and the push to the base branch triggers the workflows configured for it.

What happened instead: the squash commit landed on the base branch and the pull request stayed open and unmerged, so the history and the pull request disagreed about what had landed. The merge button on that pull request had nothing left to merge, because the base already contained the branch. No workflow ran for the commit, so the change sat on the base branch ungated.

Merging the same pull request from the website produced all three: the record flipped to merged, the `merged` event was written, and the push triggered the quality gate by itself.

### Logs

The command was not run with `GH_DEBUG=api`, so there is no request trace to attach.

```
$ gh pr merge 25 --squash --match-head-commit 4e078b84e4cd24b40847ab0b216b4140abfa5c5d --body-file commit-body.txt
$ echo $?
0

$ gh pr view 25 --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit
{"state":"OPEN","mergedAt":null,"mergeCommit":null}

$ gh api repos/pablocru/portfolio/pulls/25 --jq '{state, merged, merged_at, base: .base.sha, merge_commit_sha}'
{"state":"open","merged":false,"merged_at":null,"base":"14ca0357e5ebe5f294743895d39e366f1b4b12bc","merge_commit_sha":"e120cff96b4645e74080606a1ffd2de24d95e0ca"}

$ gh api repos/pablocru/portfolio/issues/25/timeline --jq '.[] | select(.event=="merged")'
(no output)

$ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
179415c8d3a3d578cfcd93dd86cfdaba85398ee1	refs/heads/main

$ git log -1 --format='%H %s' origin/main
179415c8d3a3d578cfcd93dd86cfdaba85398ee1 perf(ui): deliver the avatar eagerly and at the display density (#25)

$ gh run list --branch main --limit 3
completed success 14ca0357 chore(deps): update the node runtime to 24.22.1 (#24)
completed success 8c5f01dd docs: align the readme with the publication workflow (#23)
```

nodes.title: Investigate reducing Windows test-runner time through better caching
nodes.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I think we can reduce Windows test-runner time by improving reuse of Go build artifacts.

The Windows race-test job failed to save its cache because the key had already been reserved:

```shell
$ gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/cli/cli/actions/jobs/120072805549/logs | rg 'Cache is not found|Failed to save'
2026-10-22T20:33:42.2167267Z Cache is not found
2026-10-22T20:41:00.8761645Z Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key setup-go-Windows-x64-go-1.27.3-78fa9ce8bdbe17159635de6cdb60b8f679d867cfc54100974fc19f19cdf6292b, another job may be creating this cache.
```

There are two Windows build workloads involved:

* The [`build` job](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/63837fb778d6a39f02be0ce76ff89f2bc8d74bdc/.github/workflows/go.yml#L12-L35) runs `go test -race -tags=integration ./...`, then `go build -v ./cmd/gh`.
* The [`integration-tests` job](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/63837fb778d6a39f02be0ce76ff89f2bc8d74bdc/.github/workflows/go.yml#L41-L65) runs `make`, then exercises the attestation commands against the resulting executable.

The attestation job built without `-race`, using `-trimpath`, and saved the same cache key before the race-test job finished:

```shell
$ gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/cli/cli/actions/jobs/120072805565/logs | rg 'go build -trimpath|Cache saved with the key'
2026-10-22T20:34:04.5029539Z go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X github.com/cli/cli/v2/internal/build.Date=2026-10-22 -X github.com/cli/cli/v2/internal/build.Version=ed84a97 " -o bin/gh.exe ./cmd/gh
2026-10-22T20:36:28.6170907Z Cache saved with the key: setup-go-Windows-x64-go-1.27.3-78fa9ce8bdbe17159635de6cdb60b8f679d867cfc54100974fc19f19cdf6292b
```

Go cannot reuse ordinary compiled packages as race-instrumented packages. The `-trimpath` setting also affects compilation cache entries, so these workloads need different build artifacts even when their dependencies are identical.

A later race-test job restored that cache and skipped saving its newly compiled artifacts because the key was an exact hit:

```shell
$ gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/cli/cli/actions/jobs/121619521094/logs | rg 'Cache restored from key|not saving cache'
2026-10-26T14:07:48.1819774Z Cache restored from key: setup-go-Windows-x64-go-1.27.3-78fa9ce8bdbe17159635de6cdb60b8f679d867cfc54100974fc19f19cdf6292b
2026-10-26T14:15:42.6970760Z Cache hit occurred on the primary key setup-go-Windows-x64-go-1.27.3-78fa9ce8bdbe17159635de6cdb60b8f679d867cfc54100974fc19f19cdf6292b, not saving cache.
```

I suspect the shared key is giving us successful cache restores without preserving the compilation work needed by the race-test job.

### Proposed solution

Investigate whether a cache populated by the Windows test job reduces its running time compared with the current shared cache.

Compare both approaches on fresh runners using the same source revision, Go version and test commands. Measure the cost of populating and restoring the cache as well as running the tests and building the executable.

Any proposed change should preserve race detection, test selection and failure reporting. Cached test results should not be mistaken for faster compilation.

### Additional context

I don't know how much time a workload-specific cache would save once restoration costs are included.

Measurements using an unchanged source revision would not establish the benefit across normal PR traffic. The report should state that limitation and identify any follow-up questions about cache refresh or changing source revisions.

### Expected Output

The expected output for this issue is:

* A closing comment on this issue with a report explaining the current cache keys, which jobs populate them, and whether restored artifacts match the Windows test workload.
* Measurements comparing the existing cache with a cache populated by the test job, including end-to-end runner time, cache overhead, storage costs, test equivalence and limitations.
* A recommendation for whether to change the cache strategy, with any questions about cache refresh or changing source revisions identified as follow-up work.
* Optionally, a PR implementing an improvement if the evidence supports it. A report concluding that no change is worthwhile is also a valid outcome.

nodes.title: Replace github.com/vmihailenco/msgpack/v5
nodes.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

msgpack v5.4.1 is flagged for CVE-2026-2454, and upstream has been inactive since 2023, so a fix is unlikely.

### Proposed solution

gh only uses msgpack to encode `PR_`, `U_` and `DC_` node IDs from small int arrays. A ~20-line encoder in `api` produces identical output and drops the dependency. PR: #14801.

nodes.title: `gh auth status --no-refresh` shows a misleading error for expired tokens
nodes.body:
### Describe the bug

When the active account uses an expiring OAuth token (`gh auth login --expiring`) and the access token has expired, `gh auth status --no-refresh` reports the token as invalid and suggests `gh auth refresh`. Running `gh auth status` without `--no-refresh` immediately refreshes the token and reports success, so the credential was never invalid; it had just expired.

The output is misleading in three ways:

1. It says "The token in keyring is invalid", although the token has only expired and gh can renew it automatically.
2. It suggests `gh auth refresh -h github.com`, which runs the full interactive OAuth flow again (it is meant for changing scopes). Simply dropping `--no-refresh`, or running any other gh command, is enough to renew the token.
3. It hides the expiry details (token expiry and refresh token expiry) that are shown for a healthy expiring token, so there is no hint about why the check failed.

### Affected version

`gh` v2.103.1 (trunk at `64d175234`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This is how I ran into it:

1. Logged in with an expiring token: `gh auth login --expiring`
2. Did not run any gh command for longer than the access token lifetime (about 8 hours), so the token expired.
3. Ran `gh auth status --no-refresh`, which reported the token as invalid (see below).
4. Ran `gh auth status`, which refreshed the token and reported success.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Actual:

```
$ gh auth status --no-refresh
github.com
  X Failed to log in to github.com account monalisa (keyring)
  - Active account: true
  - The token in keyring is invalid.
  - To re-authenticate, run: gh auth refresh -h github.com
  - To forget about this account, run: gh auth logout -h github.com -u monalisa
```

The JSON output already carries enough to tell that the token has expired (`refreshable` and a past `tokenExpiresAt`), but the `error` message is the raw API response:

```
$ gh auth status --json hosts --no-refresh
{
  "hosts": {
    "github.com": [
      {
        "state": "error",
        "error": "HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/)",
        "active": true,
        "host": "github.com",
        "login": "monalisa",
        "tokenSource": "keyring",
        "gitProtocol": "https",
        "refreshable": true,
        "tokenExpiresAt": "2026-10-24T17:50:55.996654037Z",
        "refreshTokenExpiresAt": "2027-04-24T09:50:54.996654037Z"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Expected: when `--no-refresh` is given and the credential is an expiring token whose expiry time has passed, `gh auth status` should say the token has expired, keep showing the expiry details, and hint at dropping `--no-refresh` to let gh refresh it. For example:

```
$ gh auth status --no-refresh
github.com
  X Token for github.com account monalisa (keyring) has expired
  - Active account: true
  - Expiring token that gh refreshes automatically
  - Token expires: 2026-10-24T17:50:55Z (expired about 1 hour ago)
  - Refresh token expires: 2027-04-24T09:50:54Z (in about 6 months)
  - To refresh it, run gh auth status without --no-refresh
```

Notes:

- If the refresh token has also expired, the hint should point at `gh auth login -h <host>` instead.
- Tokens that fail for other reasons (for example, revoked tokens) should keep the current "invalid" wording.

### Logs

The failure comes from the scope check in `buildEntry` (`pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go`): with `--no-refresh`, the expired token is sent as is, the request fails, and the entry falls into the generic `authEntryStateError` branch. `shared.AuthTokenRefreshable` matches the `gho_` prefix, which is why `gh auth refresh` is suggested.
